spec.title: Capture price and capture rate
spec.main_latex: \mathrm{CR} = \frac{\bar p^{\,\text{capt}}}{\bar p} = \frac{\sum_t p_t\, q_t \,/\, \sum_t q_t}{\frac{1}{T}\sum_t p_t}

steps.explanation: The average price a technology actually earns: each hour's price weighted by its output q in that hour.
The base price: the plain average over all T hours, what a flat 'baseload' delivery earns.
Computed from hourly Energy-Charts data. Solar earned 52 % of the base price; onshore wind 87 %, offshore wind 96 %.
of all German solar energy in 2025 was produced in hours with a negative day-ahead price.

spec.caption: Falling capture rates as a technology's share grows are called cannibalisation: every new panel produces exactly when all the others do.
